statements.venue: Press release introducing the AI Emergency Button Act
statements.quote: While AI can be a helpful tool, it is essential that humans remain in control of complex artificial intelligence systems,
statements.context: Kean introduced the AI Emergency Button Act, which would require developers of advanced AI systems to build in a way for a human operator to shut the system down (companion to a Senate bill by Sen. John Kennedy).
statements.reason: Says humans must stay in control of advanced AI and backs a mandatory shutdown capability, a general acknowledgment of loss-of-control risk, but names no catastrophic consequence.

statements.venue: Press release introducing the Stop Stealing Our Chips Act
statements.quote: I introduced the Stop Stealing Our Chips Act to help authorities identify and mitigate those threats.
statements.context: A bill with whistleblower incentives to stop China and other adversaries from evading export controls on advanced American AI chips.
statements.reason: About competition with China and export control enforcement, which ruling 5 places at D.

statements.venue: Press release reintroducing the LIFT AI Act
statements.quote: The LIFT AI Act establishes a strong foundation by bringing AI education into classrooms,
statements.context: A bipartisan bill with Rep. Amo to improve AI literacy in kindergarten through 12th grade.
statements.reason: About AI education and preparing students to use AI, with no acknowledgment of catastrophic risk.

slowdown.note: No statement found on slowing frontier AI development.

pause.note: No statement found on pausing frontier AI development.

intl.note: No statement found on coordinating with China on the pace of AI development; his China-related AI work is about export controls.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI. The AI Emergency Button Act requires a shutdown capability, not a ban.

record: Introduced the AI Emergency Button Act, requiring advanced AI systems to include a capability for a human operator to shut them down.
Introduced the Stop Stealing Our Chips Act with Rep. Johnson, adding whistleblower incentives to enforce export controls on advanced AI chips.
Reintroduced the LIFT AI Act with Rep. Amo to improve AI literacy in schools.
grade_reason: His strongest statement, from 2026, says it is essential that humans remain in control of advanced AI and comes with a bill requiring a shutdown switch. That is a general acknowledgment of loss-of-control risk with no catastrophic consequence named, so C (a boundary case).
notes: All seven web searches ran this time (six required plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act); none were refused. The searches found no statement by Kean on superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, a pause or slowdown, or an agreement with China on AI. No source shows he sponsored or co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, led by Rep. Casar; reported co-sponsors are Democrats), but the congress.gov co-sponsor list was not opened. The statements and record were carried over from an earlier run that opened kean.house.gov directly (press release listings October 2026 back to January 2025; about one listing page around mid-February 2025 was skipped). This run re-opened the 2026-09-24 AI Emergency Button Act release and confirmed the date and the quoted wording. Quotes were read through a page-fetch tool that returns short exact fragments; the reviewer should check the wording against the pages. Boundary call on the 2026-09-24 statement: it could be read as D under ruling 4 (AI acting on its own with no consequence stated), but it is framed as the general need for human control of advanced AI, so I chose C. Left out as out of date range: a 2024-12-11 press release in which Kean wrote to AI company CEOs about security lapses (theft of AI technology by China), which would be D anyway; the release paraphrases him rather than quoting him. The Center for AI Policy endorsed him in 2024 based on its AI safety questionnaire (not a statement in range). The Spot the Fakes Act (July 2026, AI content labels, with Gottheimer and Liccardo) would be D; no separate release was found. Hearing remarks and floor speeches were not specifically checked beyond what the searches returned.
